limitations: Only observed process lifetimes are attributed; PID/name alone is insufficient and broker-created processes remain unattributed.
Capture-end bounds without a Procmon exit are explicit limits; missing events and dropped events are not ruled out.
CreateFile success does not prove data was written. WriteFile success is an observed operation; downloaded content needs separate file/hash proof.
A successful delete disposition requests deletion; final absence and fixture chronology provide separate outcome evidence.
Process Create/Start proves launch, not successful command completion. Network operations do not establish HTTP body contents.
Registry/file mutations on task paths do not alone prove a task was registered or fired. Service/broker rows are not attributed to the specimen.
Raw command lines, registry data, arbitrary paths and CSV remain in the guest; selected fixed fields and SHA256 digests are exported.
MSI captures require their own validated harness schema and are not accepted by this native reviewer.
